# package uapolicy

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uapolicy"
```

Package uapolicy implements the encryption, decryption, signing, and signature verifying algorithms for Security Policy profiles as defined in Part 7 of the OPC-UA specifications (version 1.04, and the ECC policies of version 1.05)

```go

```

CheckCertificate reports whether the application instance certificate can be used with the security policy: an RSA policy needs an RSA key, an ECC policy a key on one of the curves the policy permits: an ECDSA key on nistP256 or nistP384 for ECC\_nistP256, ECC\_nistP256\_AesGcm and ECC\_nistP256\_ChaChaPoly, on nistP384 for ECC\_nistP384, and an Ed25519 key for ECC\_curve25519, an ECDSA key on brainpoolP256r1 or brainpoolP384r1 for ECC\_brainpoolP256r1, on brainpoolP384r1 for ECC\_brainpoolP384r1 and an Ed448 key for ECC\_curve448. Every certificate is acceptable for the None policy, which does not use it.

It checks the key type only. Trust and validity are the business of the certificate validators.

### func CreateCertificate

```go
func CreateCertificate(rand io.Reader, template, parent *x509.Certificate, pub crypto.PublicKey, priv crypto.Signer) ([]byte, error)
```

CreateCertificate creates a certificate like x509.CreateCertificate, with the key types of ParseCertificate for the subject key pub and the issuer key priv in addition to those crypto/x509 supports.

If neither key is a Brainpool or Ed448 key, it is x509.CreateCertificate. Otherwise the certificate is signed with ECDSA and SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 by the size of the issuer's curve, with PKCS #1 v1.5 and SHA-256 for an RSA issuer, or with pure EdDSA; template.SignatureAlgorithm must be unset. A missing SubjectKeyId of a CA is derived from pub as x509.CreateCertificate does (RFC 7093 §2 method 1).

### func CreateCertificateRequest

```go
func CreateCertificateRequest(rand io.Reader, template *x509.CertificateRequest, priv crypto.Signer) ([]byte, error)
```

CreateCertificateRequest creates a PKCS #10 certificate signing request like x509.CreateCertificateRequest, also for an ECDSA key on brainpoolP256r1 or brainpoolP384r1 and for an Ed448 key.

For any other key it is x509.CreateCertificateRequest. A Brainpool request is signed with ECDSA and SHA-256 or SHA-384 by the size of the curve, an Ed448 request with pure Ed448; template.SignatureAlgorithm must be unset. The signature is verified before the request is returned.

### func CreateRevocationList

```go
func CreateRevocationList(rand io.Reader, template *x509.RevocationList, issuer *x509.Certificate, priv crypto.Signer) ([]byte, error)
```

CreateRevocationList creates a CRL like x509.CreateRevocationList, also for an issuer with an ECDSA key on brainpoolP256r1 or brainpoolP384r1 or with an Ed448 key.

For any other key it is x509.CreateRevocationList. A Brainpool CRL is signed with ECDSA and SHA-256 or SHA-384 by the size of the curve, an Ed448 CRL with pure Ed448; template.SignatureAlgorithm must be unset. The issuer needs the cRLSign key usage and a subject key identifier, and a public key in issuer, if set, must be the key of priv. The signature is verified before the CRL is returned.

EncodePFX encodes a private key and its certificates (DER) as a PKCS #12 file protected with the password, as OpenSSL 3 does by default: the key in a pkcs8ShroudedKeyBag and the certificates in encryptedData, both with PBES2 (PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA-256, 2048 iterations, AES-256-CBC), and an HMAC-SHA-256 MAC (2048 iterations), with random salts and IVs. The key is encoded with MarshalPrivateKey. One of the certificates must be the key's; a localKeyId attribute links it to the key.


ParsePFX decodes a PKCS #12 file (RFC 7292) with the password and returns its private key and its certificates. The file must hold exactly one private key; the certificate whose public key is the key's comes first, the others follow in the order of the file. ### func SecureChannelEnhancements

```go
func SecureChannelEnhancements(uri string) bool
```

SecureChannelEnhancements reports whether SecureChannels of the security policy use the enhancements of OPC UA 1.05.07 (Part 6 §6.7.5 and §6.8.1, Part 4 §6.1.8):

  - the signature of the first OpenSecureChannel response also covers the signature of the request and becomes the ChannelThumbprint;
  - a renewal derives its keys from the new shared secret combined with the key material of all earlier exchanges;
  - the signatures of CreateSession and ActivateSession cover the ChannelThumbprint, which binds a Session to its SecureChannel.

### func Thumbprint

```go
func Thumbprint(c []byte) []byte
```

Thumbprint returns the SHA-1 thumbprint of the leaf certificate in a DER-encoded certificate (or certificate chain). The thumbprint identifies the application instance certificate whose private key the peer holds, so it must be computed over the leaf only — not the whole chain. If the blob cannot be parsed as a certificate, it falls back to hashing the raw bytes to preserve the previous behavior.

### func VerifyCertificate

```go
func VerifyCertificate(certs []*x509.Certificate, roots *x509.CertPool, anchors []*x509.Certificate) error
```

VerifyCertificate verifies a certificate chain as an OPC UA application does (Part 4 §6.1.3): certs\[0] is the certificate to verify, the others are candidate intermediates. Certificates are parsed with ParseCertificate.

roots are the trust anchors for (\*x509.Certificate).Verify, which verifies every chain without Ed448 signatures, those with Brainpool keys included. crypto/x509 cannot verify an Ed448 signature: a chain in which a certificate is signed with Ed448 is verified against anchors instead, which should hold the same certificates as roots (system roots aside, which never carry Ed448 keys), with these rules of RFC 5280 §6.1: every certificate is valid at the current time and has no unknown critical extension; every issuer is a CA (basicConstraints) whose key usage, if present, includes keyCertSign and whose path length constraint holds; names chain issuer to subject and key identifiers match where both are present. A CA with name constraints is not accepted on that path. A certificate that is itself a trust anchor is trusted.

Any extended key usage is accepted.

### type ECDSA

```go
type ECDSA struct {
	Hash       crypto.Hash
	PublicKey  *ecdsa.PublicKey
	PrivateKey crypto.Signer
}
```

ECDSA implements the AsymmetricSignatureAlgorithm\_ECDSA-SHA2-\* algorithms of the ECC security policies.

OPC UA does not use the ASN.1 DER signature encoding of X.509 and TLS. A signature is the concatenation r || s, each value a big-endian integer zero-padded to the size of the curve's field (Part 6 §6.8.1, Part 7): 64 bytes for P-256 and 96 bytes for P-384.

PrivateKey is a crypto.Signer so the application instance key may live in an HSM or a key agent; only its public key has to be an \*ecdsa.PublicKey.


Signature returns the r || s encoded signature of msg.


Verify checks the r || s encoded signature of msg.

```go
type EncryptionAlgorithm struct {

```

EncryptionAlgorithm wraps the functions used to return the various methods required to implement the symmetric and asymmetric algorithms Function variables were used instead of an interface to make better use of policies which implement the same algorithms in different combinations

EncryptionAlgorithm should always be instantiated through calls to SecurityPolicy.Symmetric() and SecurityPolicy.Asymmetric() to ensure correct behavior.

The zero value of this struct will use SecurityPolicy#None although using in this manner is discouraged for readability.

Asymmetric returns the asymmetric encryption algorithm for the given security policy.

It takes RSA keys and is kept for compatibility; AsymmetricKeys accepts the keys of every supported policy, including the ECC ones.

#### func AsymmetricKeys

```go
func AsymmetricKeys(uri string, localKey crypto.PrivateKey, remoteKey crypto.PublicKey) (*EncryptionAlgorithm, error)
```

AsymmetricKeys returns the asymmetric algorithm for the given security policy: the algorithm that secures OpenSecureChannel messages and creates and verifies the signatures of CreateSession and ActivateSession.

localKey is the private key of the local application instance (or user) certificate and remoteKey the public key of the peer's certificate. Either may be nil when only the other direction is needed. The key types must match the policy: RSA policies need an \*rsa.PrivateKey and an \*rsa.PublicKey, the ECC policies a crypto.Signer with an \*ecdsa.PublicKey on a curve the policy permits and an \*ecdsa.PublicKey, ECC\_curve25519 a crypto.Signer with an ed25519.PublicKey and an ed25519.PublicKey, and ECC\_curve448 the same with ed448.PublicKey (github.com/cloudflare/circl/sign/ed448).

#### func (EncryptionAlgorithm) OpenChunk

```go
func (e *EncryptionAlgorithm) OpenChunk(chunk []byte, headerLength int, tokenID, lastSequenceNumber uint32, encrypted bool) ([]byte, error)
```

OpenChunk verifies and, if encrypted, decrypts a chunk made by the peer's SealChunk. It returns the chunk without its tag: the header followed by the plain data. The tag is compared in constant time; a chunk that was modified, truncated, replayed or secured with other keys yields ErrInvalidCiphertext and no data.

#### func (EncryptionAlgorithm) SealChunk

```go
func (e *EncryptionAlgorithm) SealChunk(chunk []byte, headerLength int, tokenID, lastSequenceNumber uint32, encrypt bool) ([]byte, error)
```

SealChunk secures a symmetric MessageChunk of a policy with authenticated encryption.

chunk holds the complete chunk without its tag; its MessageSize field must already count the tag (SignatureLength bytes), because the header is authenticated as it is sent. headerLength is the size of the part that stays readable: the message header and the symmetric security header. tokenID and lastSequenceNumber make the nonce: the TokenId of the chunk and the sequence number of the chunk sent before it. With encrypt the data after the header is encrypted (SignAndEncrypt), otherwise the chunk is only authenticated (Sign).

The result is a new slice: the header, the (encrypted) data and the tag. SealChunk fails rather than use a nonce twice.

### type KeyExchange

```go
type KeyExchange struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

KeyExchange is one side of the key negotiation of an OpenSecureChannel exchange. It creates the nonce the side sends and, once the peer's nonce is known, the symmetric algorithm that secures the messages of the new SecurityToken.

For the RSA policies the nonce is random data and the keys are derived from both nonces with P\_SHA. For the ECC policies the nonce is an ephemeral public key and the keys are derived with HKDF from the Diffie-Hellman shared secret (Part 6 §6.8.1).

A KeyExchange is used for exactly one OpenSecureChannel exchange: opening a channel and every renewal create a new one, and with it new ephemeral keys.

#### func NewKeyExchange

```go
func NewKeyExchange(uri string, role Role) (*KeyExchange, error)
```

NewKeyExchange starts the key negotiation for the security policy.

#### func (KeyExchange) Nonce

```go
func (k *KeyExchange) Nonce() []byte
```

Nonce returns the nonce to send to the peer: the ClientNonce of the OpenSecureChannel request or the ServerNonce of the response.

#### func (KeyExchange) Symmetric

```go
func (k *KeyExchange) Symmetric(remoteNonce []byte) (*EncryptionAlgorithm, error)
```

Symmetric completes the negotiation with the nonce received from the peer and returns the symmetric algorithm for the new SecurityToken.

For an ECC policy the peer's nonce is validated as a public key on the curve of the policy; an invalid key fails the negotiation.

It is SymmetricChained for the first exchange of a channel. A renewal of a channel whose policy has SecureChannelEnhancements needs SymmetricChained.

#### func (KeyExchange) SymmetricChained

```go
func (k *KeyExchange) SymmetricChained(remoteNonce, chain []byte) (algo *EncryptionAlgorithm, next []byte, err error)
```

SymmetricChained completes the negotiation like Symmetric and links the new keys to the previous ones of the channel.

chain is the value the previous exchange on the same SecureChannel returned, or nil for the exchange that opens the channel. The result is the value for the next renewal. For the security policies with SecureChannelEnhancements it is key material: the keys of a renewed SecurityToken are derived from the new shared secret combined with that of every earlier exchange (Part 6 §6.8.1), so both sides must pass the values in step. The value is secret; it must not be logged. For every other policy chain is ignored and the result is nil.

### type Role

```go
type Role int
```

Role is the side of a SecureChannel an application is on.

```go
const (
	// RoleClient is the side that sends the OpenSecureChannel request.
	RoleClient Role = iota
	// RoleServer is the side that answers it.
	RoleServer
)
```

### type Secret

```go
type Secret struct {
	// Nonce is the nonce the sender bound the secret to: the last session
	// nonce it received. The receiver must compare it with the nonce it
	// issued; DecryptSecret does not know it.
	Nonce []byte

	// Secret is the protected value.
	Secret []byte

	// Certificate is the signing certificate named in the secret.
	Certificate []byte

	// SigningTime is when the sender created the secret.
	SigningTime time.Time
}
```

Secret is the content of a decrypted EccEncryptedSecret.
